quote: It’s a high-entropy state into which the system trends, an attractor in human psychology.
content: Routinization and cultishness are not alternatives; they are the two ways a movement stops tracking reality, and the essay is describing the second because it is the one that flatters its members. The unfalsifiability objection is answered in the essay itself, which says that the effort is observable — you can look at whether a group tolerates criticism, whether its leaders are correctable, whether members can leave — and those are checkable properties rather than a post-hoc label. The thermodynamic metaphor is a metaphor and the essay says so; the claim underneath it is that the failure mode is the default and the correction is the work.

quote: Every group of people with an unusual goal—good, bad, or silly—will trend toward the cult attractor unless they make a constant effort to resist it.
content: The essay predicted this and the annotation grants that it did. What the record establishes is that constant effort is necessary and not sufficient, which is a refinement of the essay rather than a refutation, and which the essay half-states in saying that the effort must be constant. The specification the annotation asks for is available in the same literature: the risk factors that made the difference in the cases that went wrong were charismatic leadership, communal living, total worldview and high exit costs, none of which "write self-critical essays" addresses. That is the correct lesson, and the essay is the reason anyone was looking.
